summary: This article covers the five named oceans, how much of Earth's surface is covered by salt water, and why oceans shape our climate, weather, and trade.
introduce: Read the title “Oceans: The Blue Majority of Earth” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: the usual weather a place has over a long time
to change from a liquid into a gas, often because of heat
one of the seven huge areas of land on Earth, such as Asia or Africa

challengeTerms.def: the continuous movement of something, such as water or air, around a system
having to do with the sea, ships, or sailing
to take in and hold something, such as heat, light, or liquid

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that the ocean affects your daily life, even if you live far from the coast? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how oceans help regulate Earth's climate.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review climate, evaporate, and continent, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use circulation, maritime, and absorb in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
